newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia flush with corn, diverts to Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia flush with corn, diverts to Thailand.

text.p: Indonesia is flush with corn, with an importer diverting one shipment of 60,000 tonnes to Thailand while another 120,000 tonnes were cancelled because of a lack of storage space, traders said on Tuesday.

"Corn is coming out of our ears in Indonesia at the moment," a senior trader said. "Over the last 20 days, one Panamax shipment was diverted to Bangkok, while another 90,000 tonnes were washed out and 30,000 tonnes cancelled."
"The market is carrying an inventory of about 400,000 tonnes which is sufficient for two months," he said.
Traders said corn prices were generally stable on the back of ample stocks and arrival of imports, especially from China.
Corn was quoted at 380 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 380-385 rupiah a week ago. Soymeal was firmer at 900 rupiah/kg, compared 850-860 rupiah last week.
"I heard one feedmill was about to take delivery of 10,000 tonnes of Chinese corn, while another was expecting a shipment of 20,000 tonnes, also from China," one trader said.
"The continued arrival of imports is putting pressure on local corn prices, and some players are not keen on selling at the current prices," he added.
Another trader said a feedmill was taking delivery of 60,000 tonnes of South American maize and he expected some 150,000 tonnes of South American maize to arrive in July.

"The imports were apparently ordered nearly 10 months ago in forward deals in anticipation of increased domestic demand," he said. "But there have been some delays in getting new plants or upgraded ones up and running on schedule."
"There's one plant in Serang that has increased its capacity, while another company is expecting to start running a new one also in Serang in October," he added.
Another trader said he expected corn imports in the third quarter of this year to total 150,000 tonnes, adding that imports could touch 500,000 tonnes between July and December.

He said Chinese corn was being offered at $135-$136 a tonne C&F for volumes of 20,000 tonnes, while smaller volumes were quoted at $140. U.S. and South American corn were being offered at $148 and $150 a tonne respectively.
The traders said South American soymeal was being offered at $305 a tonne C&F while Indian was quoted at $348 C&F.
"The soymeal situation in Indonesia seems to be balanced at the moment...there's no oversupply like corn," one said. "Local prices are firm as demand remains good."
